record.paper_title: Billiard dynamics: A survey with the emphasis on open problems
record.original_question: Does every rational polygon have quadratic asymptotics for its periodic-strip counting function, meaning that f_P(ℓ)/ℓ^2 converges to a limit as ℓ→∞?

evidence.quote: Задача 13. Всякий ли рациональный многоугольник имеет квадратичную асимптотику?

artifact.status_search_result: Quadratic upper and lower bounds for the periodic-strip counting function in rational polygons are known (Masur), and existence of the limit (quadratic asymptotics) has been established in special cases such as Veech surfaces and regular polygons. However, no general result is known guaranteeing that f_P(ℓ)/ℓ² converges for every rational polygon; the question remains open in current surveys.

status_evidence.title: Rational billiards and flat structures (Masur–Tabachnikov)
status_evidence.snippet: In all known examples, f_P(ℓ)/ℓ² has a limit; in this case the polygon is said to have quadratic asymptotics.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of the limit is known only in special cases (e.g., Veech surfaces); the general question is open.

status_evidence.title: Survey Lecture on Billiards (Schwartz)
status_evidence.snippet: Veech computed quadratic asymptotics for regular polygons via lattice surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Quadratic asymptotics established for lattice (Veech) surfaces but not for arbitrary rational polygons.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a rational polygon, i.e., a planar polygon all of whose interior angles are rational multiples of $\pi$. Consider the billiard flow in $P$: a point particle moves in straight lines inside $P$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) off the sides. A periodic billiard trajectory in $P$ is closed; in a rational polygon every periodic trajectory belongs to a maximal parallel family (a "periodic strip") of parallel periodic trajectories of the same length, foliating an open strip in $P$.

For $\ell > 0$, define the periodic-strip counting function $f_P(\ell)$ to be the number of periodic strips in $P$ whose trajectories have length at most $\ell$. It is known that there exist constants $0 < c_*(P) \le c^*(P) < \infty$ such that for all sufficiently large $\ell$,
$$c_*(P)\,\ell^2 \;\le\; f_P(\ell) \;\le\; c^*(P)\,\ell^2.$$
One says that $P$ has quadratic asymptotics if the limit
$$\lim_{\ell \to \infty} \frac{f_P(\ell)}{\ell^2}$$
exists (and is then a positive real number).

Question: Does every rational polygon have quadratic asymptotics?
